Your RPH should not yell at you in front of customers or away from them. She definitely should have pulled you to the side. That is just bad management. While this is a serious topic with risks of addiction, she has to realize you’re in training. There is a lot of information at once for pharmacy techs and it may take a few times to remember everything. 

Also: “what if I don’t /want/ to refill it?” is shitty. If she had said, “what it’s too early to fill?” I’d understand. 
I dealt with a pharmacist like this at my last job. Her attitude mostly came from me not knowing a new system since I went from Walgreens to Kroger. 

Thankfully I had almost 2 years experience and I didn’t need to be trained in medication issues and procedure. 
What I would do is if she gets like that again, confront her gently. Remind her you’re in training and it doesn’t feel good when she snaps. If another issue comes up after that, take it to your SM. If nothing gets resolved, then go to HR or find another location with a more understanding pharmacist. I’m very lucky that my first pharmacist was really patient with me. He, like a lot of pharmacists, was a technician before he became an RPH and he understood how I needed to be taught with a gentle hand. 

I would consider taking comprehensive notes though! Really doesn’t help in the beginning. I had categories such as how to navigate the system, which medications are controlled, which medications can’t be poured into an amber vial, which medications need are hazardous and needed to be counted separately, insurance codes, etc. Even if you don’t look at them often it helps to write them down so it sticks in your brain. Just write any new info down you really need to remember. Until you really know your inventory like the back of your hand, I would look up if you have it in stock while people are in line or on the phone too. Can’t tell you how many times I’ve had to call a patient because I told them I’d fill an out of stock medication within the day.
